What We Design

Eight connected parts make the gym easy to navigate, comfortable to use and ready for hard daily wear.

01

Training Zone Planning

Equipment, circulation and safety clearances shaped around real training patterns.

02

Cardio Area Design

Comfortable spacing, strong sightlines and fresh airflow for longer sessions.

03

Strength & Free-Weight Zones

Racks, machines and lifting platforms arranged for safe, efficient movement.

04

Group Class Studios

Flexible studios for yoga, spin, HIIT or Pilates with the right floor and AV.

05

Locker Rooms & Changing Areas

Private, easy-clean spaces with practical lockers, benches and wet zones.

06

Reception & Member Lounge

A clear welcome, simple check-in and a comfortable place to pause.

07

Flooring & Acoustic Design

Impact protection and sound control matched to every activity zone.

08

Lighting & Ventilation

Bright, energising light with airflow planned for comfort at peak hours.

01 / 08

Our Design Process

Five focused stages turn your training brief into a coordinated design package.

01

Consultation & Requirements

We discuss your members, equipment, capacity, brand, budget and training mix.

02

Site Measurement

We record the floor, services, access, ventilation and structural conditions.

03

Concept & Layout Design

Cardio, strength, class and support zones form one clear member journey.

04

Material & Furniture Selection

Flooring, lighting, finishes and furniture are chosen for hard daily use.

05

Final Design Package & 3D Visualization

Drawings and 3D views prepare the gym for accurate pricing and execution.

Pricing

The initial consultation and site survey are free. We provide an exact fixed quote after the survey, once the floor area, zones and 3D package are clear.

Gym Design FAQs

Straight answers on member experience, zoning, flooring, locker rooms, timing and 3D approval.

Clear movement, comfortable spacing, good light and fresh air make training safer and more enjoyable from arrival to cooldown.

We group compatible activities, protect clear circulation and separate noisy or high-impact zones from quieter studios.

Heavy weights need impact-resistant rubber, cardio needs durable resilient flooring, and studios need finishes suited to their class type.

Yes. We plan lockers, changing areas, showers, washrooms, benches, privacy and practical wet-area finishes.

A compact gym usually takes two to three weeks. Larger clubs with several zones may take four to six weeks.

Yes. Key training zones, reception, studios and locker areas are shown in 3D before site work begins.
